title: Around the Shire: Como playground update; Heathcote Road closure; Cars sink at Yowie Bay
excerpt: Four vehicles have become wholly or partly submerged in the last two years after slipping down the Yowie...
content:
The new paddle steamer playground in Como Pleasure Grounds. Picture by Murray Trembath

Paddle steamer playground

The new $1 million Como Pleasure Grounds playground is expected to open in mid-November, subject to final compliance and safety approvals, a Sutherland Shire Council spokeswoman said.

"Final quality and safety checks are underway to ensure the playground meets all relevant Australian Standards, including requirements relating to finger entrapment risks and fall zones".

The council's original aim was to have it open by August, and that was pushed back to the end of October.

Heathcote Road closure

Heathcote Road will be closed between New Illawarra Road and Forum Drive to all traffic from 8pm on Friday November 13 until 5am Monday November 16 to allow excavation.

Work began in September on a $180 million project to add 900 metres of overtaking lane, which was promised before the 2023 state election.

There will be several more weekend closures on dates yet to be given.

A car is pulled from the water after slipping on the Yowie Bay boat ramp on October 25, 2026. Picture Facebook / Artz Micevski

Cars sink at Yowie Bay

Four vehicles have become wholly or partly submerged in the past two years after slipping down the Yowie Bay boat ramp.

However, an inspection after the latest incident on Sunday October 25 found the ramp to be "in good condition," Sutherland Shire Council said.

In response to a question on notice from Cr Melanie Gibbons, the director of infrastructure said there had been four reported incidents since 2024 of vehicles losing traction or control on the ramp.

In the first three incidents - November 2024, January 2025 and April 2025 - the vehicles became submerged.

Submerged car at the Yowie Bay ramp in November 2024. Picture Leesha Cooke

In October 2026, the vehicle was nearly submerged.

The director said an inspection at low tide after the latest incident "found the ramp to be in good condition, with programmed cleaning scheduled for the following day".

After the November 2024 incident, the council increased the scheduled cleaning frequency and progressed additional warning signs, he said.

Programmed maintenance was supplemented by reactive inspections and cleaning where required.

The director said the maintenance approach recognised the ramp's high usage, tidal environment and susceptibility to algae and marine growth, with additional works undertaken between scheduled services when conditions warranted.

"For 2026-2027, programmed cleaning is scheduled in August, October, November, December, January, February, March, April and June," he said.

"Cleaning includes high-pressure washing and the removal of algae and marine growth from the ramp surface.

"Works are undertaken at or around low tide where practicable, maximising the area of the ramp that can be safely accessed and cleaned. The timing of works can also be influenced by weather, tidal conditions and use of the facility."
